outcomes.outcome: the hashman web service runs and its backend listens on the local machine only
other machines reach hashman only through nginx over HTTPS, never the backend port
a master still running the old unit gets the localhost bind at its next agent run
the site's logos are copied from the paths in Hiera
an administrator adds a user with hashman's CLI and the role line it prints declares the user from the database
the user changes the password on the web page, through nginx, in a browser
hashman's database holds the new password, and only the new one verifies
another machine accepts the new password after its agent run against the master
the password-strength API answers OK for a strong password and NOK for a weak one, through nginx
help requests and password e-mails reach the team and the user

uncovered.why: the lab's relay host is fake, so mail leaves the master's MTA for nowhere; delivery needs a mail server the master's postfix relays to, which no baseline class installs
uncovered.lifted_by: capability: a lab mail server (on the peer) that the master's postfix relays to
uncovered.evidence: the lab Hiera's postfix_smtp_node::relayhost is a placeholder (master_fixtures.sh); no class of the repository installs a receiving mail server

outcomes.outcome: users sign data and verify signatures with the portal's key

uncovered.why: no baseline class deploys ${hashmandir}/ssl/hashman-key.pem or hashman-pubkey.pem (files/hashman/ssl ships only a public key that no manifest installs), so a site provides the key pair by hand
uncovered.lifted_by: capability: a site-provided hashman key pair (a production read or a site step, not a class)
uncovered.evidence: git ls-tree at the baseline: files/hashman/ssl holds hashman-pubkey.pem only, and no manifest names it or the private key

outcomes.outcome: with server-side session expiry on, an idle session is ended after the timeout
